question: what entering a loaded game does to each kind of battle, and what number country_intel's grants store
slots_noted: CNavalCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers and CBomberCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers are slot 19 of their classes and already recorded so; this fragment adds to their comments only.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::Enter
addresses.comment:
**What runs as a session comes up, for a new game and a loaded one alike.** Large; it walks every country of the game, and per country: UpdateTriggeredModifiers, RebuildStaticModifiers, RebuildRules, UpdateTotalLeadership, UpdateMaxManpower, UpdateIC, UpdateBlockadeLevel, UpdateAtWarAndEnemies and effective neutrality. **For a session not loaded from a save** it then calls SetUpCountryLawsAndTechnologyForNewGame (0x65B4E6 - the laws moved up and the technology bought to the start date, FINDINGS-starttech.md), reads the country's order of battle (CCountry::LoadOobFile, 0x65B4EC), calls SetUpCountryForNewGame and RecountUnitTotals, sets the shares of IC, counts the officers the units come with (0x65B651), and **sets up the build queue (0x65B749): for each line of +0xF40 it keeps the duration the file gave, calls slot 14, and sets progress to the new duration less the old, floored at 0** - so a file's `duration` is the days a line still has to go, and its `progress` and `cost` are thrown away. The arm beside it at 0x65B7C9 calls 0x4DCD70 and joins the same place; that it is a loaded session's is FINDINGS-unitstart.md's reading of the block and was not followed here. Then, for each of the country's units, what FINDINGS-unitstart.md section 6 has. The write that sets `in_game` is 0x4A92 bytes before the end. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitstart.md, section 1, and FINDINGS-buildqueue.md, section 1. **The in-game menu is made at 0x65E676-0x65EC2C**: the window `menu` (menubar.gui) through the gui's slot 11, kept at +0x1CDC and hidden, its icon `menu` given slot 33 with 1, and the six buttons of `menu_panel` attached to the glues +0x1E8 (close), +0x450 (resign), +0x4A0 (quit), +0x288 (save), +0x2D8 (message settings) and +0x378 (options), whose handlers the constructor sets (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-ingamemenu.md, section A.1).

**Load against new game, all thirteen reads of loaded_from_save (+0xD9C) read 2026-11-04** (FINDINGS-savegame.md section A.5). New game only: start_tick (+0xBE0) = tick (0x65A89B); CCountry::ActivateRankedLeaders (0x65B26D); the new-game country block (0x65B4D4, above); a unit with no name named and the starting experience (0x65B8B7); in the province pass the temperature seed, SpawnFullRevoltInProvince and the REB-province fix (0x65BF47); **the whole block at 0x65C7F0 - RebuildStrategicResourceProvinces, the weather pre-roll (not in a tutorial), AllocateProvinceIntelArrays (0x288000), the first RunDailyPass (0x65CB2E) and RunSupplyAndConvoyIterations (0x65CC64), i.e. a new game's two days and first hour**; GameStrategicWarfare_SetUpForNewGame (0x65D4C9). Loaded only: ResolveSavedFiredEvents (0x65ACA2), UpdateStrategicResources (0x65B06B), CCountry::UpdateManpowerAfterMobilising in place of the new-game block (0x65B7CA), each unit's CUnit_RefreshIntelLevel, RebuildAvatar, ShowMoving and EnterProvince (0x65B8B7), RecountBuildingProvinces (0x65CD14), CAIStrategy::RefreshTheatreProvinces(strategy, 1) and every theatre's CTheatre_StampProvinces and CTheatre_RebuildAreas (0x65D22D), **one ProcessAI for every country with a CEU3AI, unless multiplayer, theatres_dirty cleared first** (0x661935), and every loaded battle plan handed to the CBattlePlanManager (0x661A85). And UpdateAtWarAndEnemies is given loaded_from_save as its third argument (0x65B37F), so a loaded country mobilised at peace is not demobilised. Everything else in it runs for both: LoadEvents (the event files read again), each province's modifier, latitude, climate and night flag, the country rebuilds above, the neighbours, CAIStrategy::Rebuild only where the strategy is neither initialized nor static, the supply depots and CSupply::RebuildSupplyNetwork, RebuildConvoyIndexes, RemoveLandlessCountriesFromWars, RunIntelRefresh and ValidateProvinceData.

**Every battle's modifiers, read 2026-11-14** (FINDINGS-savegame.md, A.5). 0x65BBAC-0x65BBDD, for a new game and a loaded one alike: it walks the combat manager's list (CGameState +0xB5C, its `combats` at +0x8, so +0xB64) node by node and calls **slot 19, ApplyCombatModifiers, on the attacker (CCombat +0x10) with the defender and flag 0, then on the defender (+0x14) with the attacker and flag 0** - the same two calls, in the same order, as CCombat::Tick makes each hour. Every kind is on that list - land, naval, air and the bombings (a bomber side against a target side) - and nothing tests the kind, `begun` or `ended`. In a new game the walk comes before the block at 0x65C7F0, so it finds no battle; in a loaded one it finds every battle the save made. **Of the five overrides only two draw on the generator, and only while the battle's `day` (+0x1C) is under 1**: CNavalCombatant's submarine surprise (an attacking fleet with a submarine, one Random() a fleet) and CBomberCombatant's naval surprise (against a naval target, the attacking side, one Random()). `day` is saved, and after any whole round it is 1 or more, so **the only battles entering draws for are a battle at sea or a bombing of ships saved before its first round** (`day` -1).
addresses.evidence: Disassembly of 0x65BB03-0x65BBDF: `mov eax,[0x1A89790]; mov edi,[eax+0xB64]`, then per node `mov esi,[edi]; mov ecx,[esi+0x10]; mov eax,[esi+0x14]; push 0; push eax; call [vftable+0x4C]` and the mirror for +0x14 with +0x10; `mov edi,[edi+8]` to the next node. CGameState +0xB5C combat_manager and CCombatManager +0x8 combats are recorded fields. The draws: see the two ApplyCombatModifiers entries. Shown wrong by a call to slot 19 elsewhere in Enter with a flag other than 0, or by a list at +0xB64 that is not the combat manager's.
addresses.revises: the battle walk on entering, read

addresses.name: CNavalCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CNavalCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers(CNavalCombatant* this, CCombatant* other, int flag)
addresses.comment:
Slot 19 for a naval fight: per fleet and per ship, each modifier put on the ship (CSubUnit::AddCombatModifier). Poor screens (defence only), the submarines' surprise (attack only), difficulty, the ship's own experience with its pride bonus, mission efficiency, dissent, lack of supplies, wind and rain (attack only), the night (attack only, by the side's own adjuster) and the leader. **The surprise is rolled in the first round only** - an attacking fleet with a submarine, `Random() % 100 < NAVAL_COMBAT_SUB_SURPRISE_CHANCE` - and then holds while CCombat +0x1C is under NAVAL_COMBAT_SUB_SURPRISE_ROUNDS, because the function reads its own flag byte (+0x25) as the last round left it before the base clears it; a later fleet of the side shares an earlier one's success. The formulas are in reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatmods.md, section 6. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seabattle.md, section 3. **BM_LEADER_BONUS behind CUnit::LeaderHasRankForCommand inlined** - the jump table on oob_level, rank 3, 3, 2, 1, pass, then slot 15 or CLeader::CommandSize >= the regiments, pass - and skill > 0: `skill * 1000 * COMBAT_LEADER_IMPACT / 1000` on both halves, no trait. Traits by CommandEffect: 10 out_of_supply_modifier on the supply lack and 23 experience_bonus on the experience, each x (1000 + t) / 1000; 18 night_attack added to the night; none on dissent. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaairleaders.md, section 1.

**The surprise's gate, read 2026-11-14** (FINDINGS-savegame.md, A.5): the Random() at 0x566637 is reached only where the flag argument ([ebp+0xC]) is 0, this side is the attacker (+0x38), the combat's `day` (+0x1C) is under 1 (the `setl` at 0x5664CA) and the fleet has a submarine; it is drawn for **every** such fleet, whether or not an earlier fleet of the side already succeeded. CInGameIdler::Enter calls this slot on every battle with flag 0, so a battle at sea saved before its first round (`day` -1) draws here as a game is entered, and again in its first round (`day` 0). The flag byte +0x25 the surprise is carried in is not a save key (CCombatant::SaveContents), so a surprise held within NAVAL_COMBAT_SUB_SURPRISE_ROUNDS is lost on a load.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly of 0x5665F6-0x56664F: `cmp byte [ebp+0xC],0; jne`, `cmp byte [side+0x38],0; je`, `cmp byte [esp+0x11],0; je` (day < 1, set at 0x5664CA from `cmp [combat+0x1C],1; setl`), `cmp edi,ebx; jle` (submarines), then `call Random`, `% 100`, `cmp edx, NAVAL_COMBAT_SUB_SURPRISE_CHANCE/1000`. No test of the side's earlier success before the draw. Shown wrong by another path into 0x566615.

addresses.name: CBomberCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CBomberCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers(CBomberCombatant* this, CCombatant* other, int flag)
addresses.comment:
Slot 19 for the bombing side, on every wing: difficulty; **the naval surprise** (attack only: against a naval target, while the combat's `day` is under AIR_COMBAT_NAV_SURPRISE_ROUNDS, where an attacker's first round rolled under AIR_COMBAT_NAV_SURPRISE_CHANCE or the side had it the round before); **the air combat** (the sum over the battles on the unit's own list of AIR_COMBAT_ON_BOMBING x attackers / defenders of its air battles so far, each strength at least 1000); supplies; experience; mission efficiency (not under a move order); radio; dissent; **stacking** over every wing of the side, a carrier's wing over water counting CAG_STACKING_PENALTY; radar from the province and its neighbours held by a friend; the weather and the night on the attack alone; the leader. No base proximity and no fighter's bonus. Its two `+0x128` reads are CUnit::owner_id and not `air_defence` (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airdefence.md). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 8. **BM_LEADER_BONUS behind CUnit::LeaderHasRankForCommand inlined** - the jump table on oob_level, rank 3, 3, 2, 1, pass, then slot 15 or CLeader::CommandSize >= the regiments, pass - and skill > 0: `skill * 1000 * COMBAT_LEADER_IMPACT / 1000` on both halves, no trait. Traits by CommandEffect: 10 out_of_supply_modifier on the supply lack and 23 experience_bonus on the experience, each x (1000 + t) / 1000; 18 night_attack added to the night; none on dissent. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaairleaders.md, section 1.

**The naval surprise's gate, read 2026-11-14** (FINDINGS-savegame.md, A.5): the one Random() at 0x5618F7 is drawn only where the other side answers slot 9 (a naval target), the flag argument is 0, this side is the attacker (+0x38) and the combat's `day` is under 1 (0x5616CD); a success, or the side's own flag (+0x25) as the last round left it, gives the surprise while `day` is under AIR_COMBAT_NAV_SURPRISE_ROUNDS. CInGameIdler::Enter calls this slot with flag 0, so a bombing of ships saved before its first round draws here as a game is entered.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly of 0x5618A8-0x56190F: `call [other_vftable+0x24]; test al,al; je`, `cmp byte [ebp+0xC],0; jne`, `cmp byte [edi+0x38],0; je`, `cmp byte [esp+0xD],0; je` (day < 1 from 0x5616CD-0x5616D0), then `call Random`, `% 100`, `cmp edx, AIR_COMBAT_NAV_SURPRISE_CHANCE/1000; jl`. Shown wrong by another draw in the body.
addresses.revises: the naval surprise gate and entering

addresses.name: CUnit::SaveContents
addresses.comment:
**The common body of every unit block in a save**, slot 2 of the CPersistent table CUnit keeps at +8 - so `this` here is the unit + 8, and every offset below is the unit's own (the code's + 8). 0x5B8170 to the `ret 4` at 0x5B8C50. First it sets the unit's +0x49 (saved_this_pass). Then, in this order: `id` (the {id type} pair at +0x10, always); `name` (+0x16C, always, quoted); `base` = the base province's id, only where home_base_ptr (+0x98) is set and its slot 1 (IsCarrier) answers false - so an air group on a carrier and every land unit write none; `leader` {id type} where the leader (+0x12C) answers true to its slot 8 (CNullLeader answers false); `previous` (+0x134) where set; `movement_progress` (+0x14C, fixed, always); `arrow_state` (+0x18C) where not 0; `path` (the CList of province ids at +0x138, through SaveWriteIntList - nothing when empty); `location` (+0x130) where set; `retreat=yes` where +0x158 is set; `dig_in` (+0x1C8), `attack_delay` (+0xD4) and `combat_hours` (+0xD8), each only where above 0; `is_prioritized` (+0xA4), `can_reinforce` (+0xA6), `can_upgrade` (+0xA5) as yes/no and `fuel` (+0x100), `supplies` (+0xFC) as fixed, all five always. Then every brigade of +0x38 under `regiment`, `ship` or `wing` by its slots 9/10/11 (a sub unit answering none of them is not written), each by its own Save. Then the children (+0x1E4) in list order: one whose +0x49 is already set is skipped; an air unit whose base answers IsCarrier is skipped (its ship writes it); a land child carried by a fleet (CArmy +0x300) or by air (+0x304) is skipped too, because its carrier writes it - **except** that where the carrying fleet is the child itself or lies in the child's own subtree (CUnit::HasDescendant), the fleet is written here, under `navy`, in the child's place; every other child goes under the key of its oob_level (+0x1F4: theatre, armygroup, army, corps, division, navy, air; `none` for any other), written by its CPersistent Save. Then the order (+0xB0) under its own key (slot 16, GetTypeId) where its slot 24 answers true - every order class but CNullOrder. Then `start_date` (+0xCC) and `end_date` (+0xD0) as date strings, each only where its year is above 1 (not the null date); `disengage` (+0xA8) and `possible_retreat` (+0xAC) together, where disengage is above 0; `track=yes` where +0x95 (shadowed_by_patrol) is set; `was_paradropped=yes` where +0x97 is set; `plan` = the CUnitPlan at +0x1FC through its slot 1, where plan_active (+0x204) is set and oob_level is below 4; `expeditionary_owner` (the tag, quoted) and `expeditionary_date` where +0x290 is not 0; `aggression_enabled=yes` and `aggression_setting` (+0x4C, fixed) where +0x4A is set; and `country_intel`, the 12-byte entries of +0x2A8..+0x2AC flattened into one vector of ints (0x4608D0), where there are any. `is_reserve` is never written though CUnit::LoadKey reads it. Callers: CArmy::SaveContents, CNavy::SaveContents and CAir::SaveContents first thing, and this table's own slot 2.

**`country_intel`, read 2026-11-14** (FINDINGS-savegame.md, C.2): 0x5B8B7D-0x5B8C3C copies every 12-byte grant's three ints **unchanged** into a temporary vector of 3n ints (0x84AFB0 sizes it) and hands it to SaveWriteIntVector under token 0x846. Nothing is added to the first number: what the save holds is what CUnit_GrantIntel stored - the granted country's id, the countries vector's index, where 0 is the null country `---` and REB is 1. So the *measured* "place among the save's country blocks plus one" is the id itself, the writer skipping index 0.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly of 0x5B8B7D-0x5B8C3C: `(end - begin) / 12` by 0x2AAAAAAB, three `mov` pairs per entry from [this+0x2A0] (the unit's +0x2A8, `this` being the unit + 8) into the temporary, `mov ecx,0x846; call 0x4608D0`. Shown wrong by an `inc` or `add` on the first int between the copy and the call.

addresses.name: CUnit::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CUnit::LoadKey(CUnit* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment:
**The whole of what an order of battle block accepts** - a `division`, `corps`, `army`, `navy`, `air` or `theatre` - 40 keys in one switch of 4658 bytes. Seven open a child unit (`theatre`, `armygroup`, `army`, `corps`, `division`, `navy`, `air`), three say what the unit is made of (`regiment`, `ship`, `wing`, all reaching CSubUnit::LoadKey), four are identity (`id`, `name`, `location`, `leader`) and the rest is state a save carries: `path`, `track`, `previous`, `movement_progress`, `retreat`, `possible_retreat`, `disengage`, `arrow_state`, `start_date`, `end_date`, `was_paradropped`, `supplies`, `fuel`, `dig_in`, `attack_delay`, `combat_hours`, `can_upgrade`, `can_reinforce`, `is_reserve`, `is_prioritized`, `plan`, `expeditionary_owner`, `expeditionary_date`, `aggression_enabled`, `aggression_setting`, `country_intel`. The loader cannot tell an OOB file from a save - it is the same switch - so every one of them is legal in `history/units`.

**Any other key goes to CreateOrder** (the default at 0x5B7E3F): where the token is one of its 33 order kinds the new order reads the block (its slot 3) and becomes the unit's order (+0xB0), **without freeing an order already there**; anything else is dropped. That is how `strategic_redeployment`, `patrol`, `air_intercept` and the rest come back.

**A child unit**: a new CArmy (or CNavy, or CAir), +0x48 set, oob_level from the key, slot 28 with this unit's idler, the owner copied, the block read; **without a `location` it is deleted**; with one it is hung under this unit (CUnit_AttachToParent - for a land child only where this unit answers IsLand) and added to its owner's unit list. **A `regiment`, `ship` or `wing`**: a new sub unit with this unit's owner and unit_ptr (+0xB0) - a regiment also takes is_reserve where this unit's +0x96 is set, before and after its block - read, added with AddRegimentToUnit, and given a name where it has none: a ship or wing from CCountry::MakeSubUnitName, a regiment `<n>. <unit name>`. **`location`**: the province by id and CUnit::EnterProvince; outside a game loaded from a save (+0xD9C) an unknown id puts the unit in province 1 with an error and enemy ground or under 20% infrastructure only logs. The scalars land where CUnit::SaveContents reads them (`this` is the unit + 8): fixed through TokenToFixedPoint or ParseFixedPoint, `track`, `was_paradropped`, `is_prioritized`, `can_reinforce`, `can_upgrade`, `aggression_enabled` and `is_reserve` through ParseBool, `retreat` true only for the word yes, `start_date`/`end_date` through Date_SetFromString, `previous` as a province, `country_intel` as a vector re-cut into 12-byte grants.

**The keyword does not pick the class, the parent does**: CNavy::LoadKey and CAir::LoadKey take the five child-unit keywords back and send all five to one handler that still builds a CArmy. Reached from RTTI, not from the first vftable: CArmy keeps CPersistent at object offset 8, so slot 4 of its primary table is a per-unit update and not this. **`leader`** (token 0x268): a plain number is looked up as the persistent {id, type 0x25} across the whole game and put on with CUnit::SetLeader(leader, 0, 0) - no check of his country, rank or kind; a save's {id type} block goes through ParseObjectReference to the same setter. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leaderassign.md, section 3.

**`country_intel`, read 2026-11-14** (FINDINGS-savegame.md, C.2): the arm at 0x5B7EA6 reads the block with ParseIntVector into a local vector and appends `(n - 1) / 3 + 1` grants to +0x2A8 through Vector12_PushBack, each the three ints as read - **nothing subtracted from the country number**, and the unit's grants are not cleared first, so a second key appends. With a count not a multiple of three the last grant reads past the vector's end (no save has one).
addresses.evidence: Disassembly of 0x5B7EA6-0x5B7F1B: `call 0x45F450` into [esp+0x20], `lea edx,[eax-1]; mul 0xAAAAAAAB; shr esi,1; inc esi`, `lea edi,[ebx+0x2A0]` (unit +0x2A8), three loads from the local into the entry, `call 0x511E50`, step 12. Shown wrong by an arithmetic step on [ebx-8] before the copy.

addresses.name: CUnit_GrantIntel
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CUnit_GrantIntel(int countryId@stack:4, int duration@stack:8, int level@stack:0xC, CUnit* unit@EAX)
addresses.comment:
**What fills CUnit +0x2A8**, the list FINDINGS-airbattle.md found the intel pass reading but nobody writing: a vector of 12-byte `{country id, duration, level}`. Finds the entry for countryId and overwrites its duration and level - **a lower level replaces a higher** - or appends one (0x111E50). CUnit::UpdateDaily takes one off every entry's duration each call and removes it at 0. **Two callers**: CLocalIntelBoost::Execute (0x9BE641, level 8, SPY_MILITARY_INTEL_LOCAL_TIME_BASE) and CSpyPresence::RunMilitaryEspionage (0x530076, level 2..9, SPY_MILITARY_INTEL_TIME_BASE).

**The country number is the tag's id** (read 2026-11-14, FINDINGS-savegame.md, C.2): RunMilitaryEspionage pushes `[actor+4]`, the id half of the actor's CCountryTag (0x53006F), and CLocalIntelBoost::Execute pushes the scope's FROM id at +0x1C (0x9BE62D). It is stored as given, and CUnit::SaveContents and CUnit::LoadKey copy it unchanged as the first of `country_intel`'s triples.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly of 0x530068-0x530076 and 0x9BE627-0x9BE641: the pushed first argument is the tag's +4, the id; 0x5D40BE stores it as the entry's first int. Shown wrong by a caller pushing a different number.
addresses.revises: the country number is the id

addresses.name: ParseIntVector
addresses.comment: **Reads a block of integers and appends each to a std::vector<int>.** 0x45F450 to the `ret 8` at 0x45F5DD. Token by token from the parse context's reader (+0x1C) until a close brace (type 4) or the end (0x13); each token's text is converted by sscanf with **`%i`** - so a leading `0x` reads as hex and a leading `0` as octal - and push_back onto `out` (growing by half, `vector<T> too long` past 0x3FFFFFFE). **It does not clear `out`**, so a caller that does not empty the vector first appends: a unit's second `country_intel` does, and it fits the country's `cabinet` key at 0x4CEB73, whose appending the CCountry cabinet field's comment infers. Callers include CUnit::LoadKey (0x5B7EC8, `country_intel`). The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly of the whole body: `[ebp+8]` the parse context, `[ebp+0xC]` the vector, the format at 0x15FD14C reads `%i`, the push_back inlined at 0x45F4F9-0x45F565, `ret 8`. Shown wrong by a clear of the vector at entry.

addresses.name: Vector12_PushBack
addresses.comment: **std::vector<T>::push_back for a 12-byte element**, the element pointer in EAX and the vector in EDI, a bare `ret` (0x511EA0 and 0x511EC7, one arm for an element inside the vector's own storage). Grows the vector when full, copies 8 bytes by movq and the last 4, and adds 12 to the end. Five callers, among them CUnit::LoadKey (0x5B7F10, `country_intel`) and CUnit_GrantIntel (0x5D40C4). The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly of 0x511E50-0x511EC7: [edi]/[edi+4]/[edi+8] begin/end/capacity, `add dword [edi+4],0xC`, bare `ret` twice; findRefs.py --callers lists five direct calls. Shown wrong by a stack argument read.

struct_fields.name: intel_grants
struct_fields.comment: Begin of a vector of 12-byte `{country id, duration, level}` entries: the intel pass gives each listed country at least that level on the province the unit stands in while the duration is above 0 (FINDINGS-airbattle.md). Filled by CUnit_GrantIntel, whose caller is `local_intel_boost` (level 8, SPY_MILITARY_INTEL_LOCAL_TIME_BASE). **Saved and loaded unchanged as `country_intel`** (read 2026-11-14, CUnit::SaveContents and CUnit::LoadKey): the first int is the granted country's tag id - REB 1, the null country 0 - so in a save it reads as the country's place among the country blocks plus one.
struct_fields.evidence: The copies at 0x5B8BF0-0x5B8C14 and 0x5B7EF8-0x5B7F10 move the three ints with no arithmetic.
